Ticket Id: 28561

Dr L Roberts

Admitting Officer

Newtown Hospital

1 Main Street

Newtown

10-02-2014

Dear Dr Roberts,

RE: Mrs May Hong                           DOB: 1971

I am writing to refer Mrs Hong, a 43-year-old patient whose, features are suggestive of right lower lobar
pneumonia for urgent admission.

Mrs Hong is a smoker. She has been suffering from mitral regurgitation and atrial fibrillation as a
consequence of rheumatic carditissince childhood.                                                            Commented [JG1]: carditis since

On 07-02-2014, Mrs Hong presented with a 3-day history of productive cough associated with fever. Her
chest examination revealed scattered rhonchi and apical systolic murmur. Acute bronchitis was the
provisional diagnosis. Accordingly, amoxycillin was prescribed in addition to her usual medication. I also
advised her to quit smoking. 2 days later, her temperature increased to 38.5. Moreover, mild crackles were
detected at the right lung base posteriorly which suggested early right basal pneumonia.

On today's review, Mrs Hong's condition deteriorated and she developed pleuritic right sided chest pain
associated with dyspnea. On examination, I detected right lower lobe dullness in addition to the previous
crackles. The heart murmur was loader associated with high rate (110/minute). Laboratory results showed      Commented [JG2]: louder
leukocytosis and amoxicillin resistance. Chest X-ray revealed right lower lobe opacity.

In view of the above, I would appreciate your further assessment and management.

Should you require any more questions, please do not hesitate to contact me.                                 Commented [JG3]: have

Yours sincerely

Doctor
